newsitem.title: USA: IBM has 55 firms in virtual industrial park.
newsitem.headline: IBM has 55 firms in virtual industrial park.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said 55 small companies have joined its Web site for small businesses, which it compared to a "virtual industrial park."
The Web site, called World Distributor, is a secure site where small businesses can find and buy products, parts, machines and tools to run their business, the computer giant said on Tuesday.
The site, started in September as a pilot programme in conjunction with the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors, is like a "virtual industrial park," IBM said.
The only cost a company has is to maintain its own Web site, which is linked to the IBM World Distributor site.
IBM provides technology -- known as secure encryption -- that enables companies to make purchases safely.
One small company, Carlson Systems of Omaha, Nebraska, is using World Distributor to enter new markets, reduce its cost of sales and improve its order processing, IBM said.

Full-colour customer catalogues are available online in areas including capital goods, chemicals, computer equipment, construction, consumer goods, foods and beverages, industrial parts and equipment, medical, metal and other categories.
